correctness.rationale: For every finite space with induced seven-antihole, twin quotient retains seven distinct non-twin vertices. Seven distance-three graph edges belong to pairwise incompatible maximal cliques and force seven distinct minimal common lower bounds outside the seven induced vertices. At the 14-point bound, equal-size distinct closed neighborhoods exclude order comparisons among the seven induced points. Each minimal witness can dominate its two forced endpoints and optionally the unique third vertex. The remaining edges are present exactly when the optional-index subset covers the step-two C7. All 128 choices are checked; 29 covers split into five D7 orbits. Height-one order complexes are connected 14-vertex, (14+|S|)-edge graphs, hence bouquets of |S|+1 circles and finite spaces are weakly equivalent via McCord. The proof covers arbitrary finite spaces, not just enumerated models.

The new claim is the **complete classification of minimizers**, not merely sharpening the bound.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the all-equality-cases classification, five isomorphism types, and weak homotopy ranks. The numerical seven-cover theorem and fourteen-point minimum are already implied by Kim–Park–Sano (2009) and general finite-space theorems of Cameron–Kumar (2026), so neither is claimed as an independently new result. residual_risks: The 2009 graph covering theorem makes the 14-point cardinality threshold a prior-implied consequence; novelty must not be attributed to that number alone.

The 1966 finite-space weak equivalence is known; only computation of the order complex and ranks is specific to this classification.

value.rationale: This is a motivated natural complete extremal classification for the first genuine odd antihole, arising explicitly from a contemporary graph-of-topology problem. Beyond the already-known covering number, it determines every 14-point finite-space specialization poset, the five homeomorphism types and four distinct weak homotopy types. Two nonhomeomorphic equality models have the same six-circle weak type, sharpening the distinction between homeomorphism and weak homotopy. The cyclic cover structure and rigidity proof make this substantially more informative than re-evaluating a known graph parameter.
